title: HeaderDateTime::tz_before_gmt is a bool that is really a two-variant Sign enum
description: header_typed.rs:76 exposes `pub tz_before_gmt: bool` as a public field. The rubric's textbook example: a bool parameter/field that is really a two-variant enum in disguise. At a call site like `HeaderDateTime { tz_before_gmt: true, tz_hour: 5, .. }` the reader cannot tell whether `true` means 'west of GMT' or 'east of GMT' without looking at the doc comment. Idiomatic Rust would expose `pub tz_sign: TzSign` where `enum TzSign { East, West }` (or similar), making the meaning self-documenting at every construction and pattern-match. Distinct from MIME-o2c.10 (which is about mirroring mail-parser's representation generally); even if the crate intentionally mirrors mail-parser internally, the public surface does not have to inherit the bool. Note: this is also a serde wire-format change if fixed after publish, so it should be settled before 1.0.
close_reason: HeaderDateTime cleanup batch: (.31) tz_before_gmt bool replaced with TzSign enum (East/West); (.9) field invariants documented per field, plus type-level statement that out-of-range values yield unspecified output; (.10) wire-format dependency on mail-parser made explicit with a doc section; (.15) to_rfc3339 doc specifies exact output (Zulu Z for UTC, ±HH:MM otherwise) with examples and out-of-range escape hatch; (.16) to_timestamp doc specifies pre-epoch / out-of-range behaviour. Struct gains #[non_exhaustive]. New test pins Zulu-form output for UTC.
